assets.strategy_rationale: The spec explicitly states 'Use plain coloured squares only; no images or sounds.', so all graphics will be drawn procedurally.

grid_system.detail: The game operates on a discrete 20x20 grid. All positions for the snake and food are integer coordinates within this grid. Rendering will scale these grid coordinates to pixel positions on the screen.

architecture.test_input_example: Press RIGHT for 5 seconds, then UP for 2 seconds, then LEFT for 3 seconds, then DOWN for 2 seconds. Repeat until game over. Press R to restart. Press ESC to quit.

decisions.reason: The spec describes a single snake and controls, with no mention of multiple players, so it's assumed to be a single-player game.
A 20x20 grid with 30x30 pixel squares gives 600x600 for the game area. An additional 80 pixels height is added for the score and controls display at the top and bottom.

A frame rate of 10 FPS provides a steady, classic Snake game pace where the snake moves one square per frame, which feels appropriate for a 'steady pace' without being too fast or too slow for a 20x20 grid.

decisions.choice: Grid coordinates (9, 9), (10, 9), (11, 9) with head at (11, 9) moving right.
decisions.reason: For a 20x20 grid (0-19), the 'middle' is around index 9 or 10. Starting with the head at (11,9) and body segments at (10,9) and (9,9) ensures it's centered and immediately moves right as specified.

decisions.choice: Green for snake, Red for food, Black for background, White for text.
decisions.reason: Standard color choices for classic Snake games and good contrast for readability.
The spec says 'controls below it' (referring to the score). Placing the score at the top and controls at the bottom is a common and clear layout.
